applies_why: The judge text is deciding a collision between the challenger's chain and the defender's chain and explicitly assesses each as footed.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: “never verse by verse” — one reading forbids using the absence of an explicit verse naming Joseph as a defect; the other treats such absence as a footing issue.
why: The judge calls the challenger's chain footed but then faults it for not naming Joseph, applying an explicit-statement/verse-level test rather than weighing chain footing as K-C requires.
